senses.d: Not in danger; out of harm's reach.
ex: You’ll be safe from the storm here in the cabin.

senses.d: Free from risk.
ex: It’s safe to eat this berry.

senses.d: Providing protection from danger; providing shelter.
ex: We have to find a safe spot, where we can hide out until this is over.

senses.d: When a batter successfully reaches first base, or when a baserunner successfully advances to the next base or returns to the base he last occupied; not out.
ex: The pitcher attempted to pick off the runner at first, but he was safe.

senses.d: In a location that renders it difficult to pot.

ex: If you push it to the limit, safety is not guaranteed.

senses.d: A safety lock or safety catch: a mechanism on a weapon or dangerous equipment designed to prevent accidental firing or operation.

senses.d: Preservation from escape; close custody.
ex: […] imprison him, […] / Deliver him to safety; and return,

senses.d: An instance of a player being sacked or tackled in the end zone, or stepping out of the end zone and off the field, resulting in two points to the opposite team.
ex: He sacked the quarterback in the end zone for a safety.

senses.d: Any of the defensive players who are in position furthest from the line of scrimmage and whose responsibility is to defend against passes as well as to be the tacklers of last resort.
ex: The free safety made a game-saving tackle on the runner who had broken past the linebackers.

senses.d: A safety squeeze.
A safety shot or sequence of such shots.
